title: What might have been
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte + , + wäre ich gekommen

rules.text: ONE PAST SUBJUNCTIVE, NOT TWO. English needs two constructions for the unreal past — if I had known, I would have come — and German has a single one: the Perfekt with its auxiliary moved into Konjunktiv II. hätte … gemacht, wäre … gekommen. Every participle is already yours from L1-M5 and L2-M10, and the haben/sein split is L2-M10's rule doing its fourth job: what moves or changes state takes wäre, everything else takes hätte.

THE UMLAUT IS THE MOOD, not decoration. hatte is the real past (L1-M5) and hätte is the unreal one (L3-M4); war against wäre, konnte against könnte. They are two different index keys, because the fold keeps the umlaut, and they say two different things: Wenn ich Zeit hatte is a habit you had, Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte is a time that never came. Write the umlaut or write another sentence.

THE AUXILIARY GOES LAST IN THE WENN-CLAUSE. English puts had in front of the participle; German puts the participle first and the auxiliary behind it, because wenn is subordinating and the finite verb is last (L1-M9). Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte, never *wenn ich hätte Zeit gehabt. In the main half the finite verb is second as always, and after a fronted wenn-clause that means wäre ich gekommen.

THE DOUBLE INFINITIVE (Ersatzinfinitiv). When a modal joins the past subjunctive it does NOT appear as a participle. Ich hätte kommen können, never *ich hätte kommen gekonnt. Das hättest du sagen sollen. The clause ends with TWO INFINITIVES — the full verb first, the modal second — and the finite hätte stands in position two. That is the exact reverse of English should have come, and it is the one thing from this module to over-learn.

THE ONE PLACE VERB-FINAL BENDS. In a subordinate clause the finite verb of a double infinitive moves in FRONT of the pair instead of standing last: Ich weiß, dass ich hätte kommen können — not *dass ich kommen können hätte. It is the single exception to L1-M9's verb-final law in the whole course, it applies only to a double infinitive, and it is named here rather than drilled.

WÜRDE BUILDS NO PAST, and what stays elsewhere. English would have is two words; German is one, wäre or hätte, so *ich würde gekommen sein is not a sentence anybody says. The present Konjunktiv II — wäre, hätte, könnte, sollte, müsste, würde — is L3-M4's and is used here freely without a new row. Konjunktiv I is L4-M7's, the narrative Präteritum L4-M8's. And a fact that was NOT undone stays in the plain Perfekt: Schade, dass ich nicht mitgekommen bin. Only the unreal half takes the mood.

sentences.display: Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte, wäre ich gekommen
sentences.cue: If I had had time, I would have come
sentences.literal: If I time had-had would-have, would-be I come

words.note: The participle of haben. In a wenn-clause it stands BEFORE its auxiliary — gehabt hätte — which is the reverse of English had had.

sentences.trap: Wenn ich Zeit hatte means whenever I had time — a habit. The umlaut of hätte is what makes the time unreal, and it is never optional.
sentences.sound: ven ikh TSAIT ge-HAPT HET-uh, VAIR-uh ikh ge-KOM-un.

variations.display: Wenn wir Zeit gehabt hätten, wären wir gekommen
variations.cue: If we had had time, we would have come
variations.changed: Plural throughout: hätten in the wenn-clause, wären in the main half. The order of both halves is untouched.

mistake.display: Wenn ich Zeit hatte, wäre ich gekommen
mistake.why: hatte is the real past, so the first half now reports something that did happen while the second half denies it. The unreal past needs hätte: Wenn ich Zeit gehabt hätte.

sentences.usage: Explaining after the fact why you did not turn up.
sentences.mnemonic: gehabt hätte — the doing first, the mood last.

sentences.display: Ich hätte früher Bescheid sagen sollen
sentences.cue: I should have let you know earlier
sentences.literal: I would-have earlier notice say should

words.cue: notice, word (as in let someone know)
words.note: Bescheid sagen is a fixed pair: to let somebody know. Bescheid takes no article and does not move: Ich sage Ihnen Bescheid.

sentences.trap: English should have said puts the modal first. German puts it LAST, behind the full verb: sagen sollen, and never *gesollt.
sentences.sound: ikh HET-uh FRUE-er buh-SHAIT ZAA-gun ZOL-un.

variations.display: Ich hätte früher Bescheid sagen müssen
variations.cue: I would have had to let you know earlier
variations.changed: sollen becomes müssen — the obligation hardens from ought to had to. The double-infinitive order does not move.

mistake.display: Ich hätte früher Bescheid sagen gesollt
mistake.why: A modal in the past subjunctive appears as an infinitive, not a participle. The pair is sagen sollen; gesollt is a form this construction has replaced.

sentences.usage: Apologising for having kept somebody waiting on news.
sentences.mnemonic: Two infinitives at the end, the modal riding last.

sentences.display: Das hättest du mir sagen können
sentences.cue: You could have told me that
sentences.literal: That would-have you to-me say can

words.note: The du-form of hätte (L3-M4). Umlaut and two t's: hättest is the unreal one, hattest the plain past you never need here.

sentences.trap: English could have told is modal, auxiliary, participle. German is auxiliary, full verb, modal — hättest … sagen können — with the modal at the very end.
sentences.sound: das HET-est doo MEER ZAA-gun KOEN-un.

variations.display: Das hätten Sie mir sagen können
variations.cue: You could have told me that
variations.changed: The same reproach to somebody you address as Sie. hättest becomes hätten; nothing else in the clause moves.

mistake.display: Das hättest du mir sagen gekonnt
mistake.why: können keeps its infinitive shape here. gekonnt exists, but not behind another infinitive: the pair is sagen können.

sentences.usage: A mild reproach to a friend who kept something back.
sentences.mnemonic: hättest … können — the blame opens and the modal closes.

sentences.display: Fast wäre ich zu spät gekommen
sentences.literal: Almost would-be I too late come

words.note: fast means almost and never English fast (that is schnell, L2-M9). It marks a near miss, so the clause behind it is unreal.
zu here is too, not to: zu spät is too late. The pair is fixed and takes no ending — Sie kommen zu spät.

sentences.trap: fast fronts, so the finite verb follows it immediately: Fast wäre ich. English almost I would have keeps the subject in front; German does not.
sentences.sound: fast VAIR-uh ikh tsoo SHPAIT ge-KOM-un.

variations.display: Beinahe wäre ich zu spät gekommen
variations.cue: I very nearly arrived too late
variations.changed: beinahe for fast — the same near miss, one degree more deliberate. Both front and both invert.

mistake.display: Fast ich wäre zu spät gekommen
mistake.why: Whatever stands first, the finite verb is second: Fast wäre ich. Putting ich between them gives the verb a third seat, which German does not have.

sentences.usage: The friendliest sentence in the module — a near miss that ended well.
sentences.mnemonic: fast fronts, wäre follows, the subject waits its turn.

sentences.display: Es wäre besser gewesen, wenn wir gewartet hätten
sentences.cue: It would have been better if we had waited
sentences.literal: It would-be better been, if we waited would-have

words.note: The participle of sein. wäre gewesen is would have been in two words where English needs three — the auxiliary alone carries the mood.
Regular participle of warten (L3-M4): ge- + wart + -et. warten takes haben, so the unreal past is hätten gewartet, never wären.

sentences.trap: The wenn-clause ends gewartet hätten. An author who writes *wenn wir hätten gewartet has used the double-infinitive order on a clause that has no modal in it.
sentences.sound: es VAIR-uh BES-er ge-VAY-zun, ven veer ge-VAR-tet HET-un.

variations.display: Es wäre besser gewesen, wenn wir gefragt hätten
variations.cue: It would have been better if we had asked
variations.changed: One participle swaps for another. gefragt also takes haben, so hätten stays.

mistake.display: Es wäre besser gewesen, wenn wir hätten gewartet
mistake.why: wenn sends the finite verb to the very end: gewartet hätten. The auxiliary only jumps in front of a DOUBLE INFINITIVE, and there is no modal here.

sentences.usage: Reviewing a decision with the people who took it with you.
sentences.mnemonic: besser gewesen — the judgement, then the participle that carries it.

sentences.display: Wenn ich das doch nur gewusst hätte
sentences.cue: If only I had known that
sentences.literal: If I that yet only known would-have

words.note: The participle of wissen, and it is irregular: gewusst, not *gewisst. Wenn ich das gewusst hätte is the standard German regret.

sentences.trap: doch nur is what carries if only; there is no separate word for only-if. Both halves are already yours — doch is L1-M2's and nur is L3-M10's.
sentences.sound: ven ikh das dokh NOOR ge-VUST HET-uh.

variations.display: Wenn wir das doch nur gewusst hätten
variations.cue: If only we had known that
variations.changed: Plural subject, so hätte becomes hätten. doch nur keeps its seat in the middle field.

mistake.display: Wenn ich das doch nur hätte gewusst
mistake.why: The clause has no modal, so the finite verb stays at the end: gewusst hätte. Moving hätte forward is the double-infinitive order borrowed where it does not belong.

sentences.usage: A wish about something you could not have known at the time.
sentences.mnemonic: doch nur — two small words and the whole regret.

sentences.display: Schade, dass ich nicht mitgekommen bin
sentences.cue: It is a shame that I did not come along
sentences.literal: Shame, that I not along-come am

words.note: A whole regret in one word: Schade! On its own, or in front of a dass-clause. It takes no ending and no article.
Participle of mitkommen (L3-M1). The ge- goes INSIDE, between prefix and stem — mitgekommen, never *gemitkommen — and it takes sein.

sentences.trap: This one is NOT subjunctive. Not coming along really happened, so it stays in the plain Perfekt; only the half that did not happen takes the mood.
sentences.sound: SHAA-duh, das ikh nikht MIT-ge-kom-un bin.

variations.display: Schade, dass wir nicht mitgekommen sind
variations.cue: It is a shame that we did not come along
variations.changed: Plural subject, so bin becomes sind. dass still parks the verb at the end.

mistake.display: Schade, dass ich nicht mitgekommen wäre
mistake.why: wäre would make the staying-behind unreal, and it was real. A fact is reported in the Perfekt; the subjunctive is for what never happened.

sentences.usage: Saying you are sorry to have missed something, without blaming anyone.
sentences.mnemonic: Schade is for what happened; hätte is for what did not.

sentences.display: Das war mein Fehler, es tut mir leid
sentences.cue: That was my mistake, I am sorry
sentences.literal: That was my mistake, it does to-me sorrow

words.note: der Fehler, and the plural is die Fehler — the noun itself does not change. einen Fehler machen is the pair for making one.

sentences.trap: es tut mir leid is one frozen phrase and mir is dative: the sorrow is done TO me. Every word of it is already yours from L2-M1.
sentences.sound: das vaar main FAY-ler, es toot meer LAIT.

variations.display: Das war mein Fehler, das tut mir wirklich leid
variations.cue: That was my mistake, I am really sorry
variations.changed: wirklich sharpens the apology and sits in the middle field, in front of leid.

mistake.why: The mistake was real, so it takes war. wäre gewesen would say it would have been my mistake — a hypothetical you are not owning.

sentences.usage: Owning a mistake plainly, which German expects you to do in one sentence.
sentences.mnemonic: war for what was; the mood is only for what was not.

sentences.display: Beinahe wärst du zu spät gekommen
sentences.cue: You very nearly arrived too late
sentences.literal: Nearly would-be you too late come

words.note: The fuller twin of fast and the same near miss. It fronts and inverts: Beinahe wärst du zu spät gekommen.
The du-form of wäre (L3-M4). kommen is a verb of motion, so its unreal past takes wärst, never hättest.

sentences.trap: The auxiliary is chosen by the full verb, not by the mood. kommen took sein in L2-M10, so it takes wärst here — hättest gekommen is not a thing.
sentences.sound: bai-NAA-huh VAIRST doo tsoo SHPAIT ge-KOM-un.

variations.display: Beinahe wären Sie zu spät gekommen
variations.cue: You very nearly arrived too late
variations.changed: The same near miss said to somebody you address as Sie: wärst becomes wären.

mistake.display: Beinahe hättest du zu spät gekommen
mistake.why: kommen takes sein, so the unreal past is wärst gekommen. The umlaut is right; the auxiliary is the wrong one.

sentences.usage: Teasing a friend who made it by seconds.
sentences.mnemonic: Motion takes wäre — even when the motion never quite happened.

sentences.display: Ich hätte Ihnen gern geholfen, aber ich hatte keine Zeit
sentences.cue: I would gladly have helped you, but I had no time
sentences.literal: I would-have to-you gladly helped, but I had no time

words.note: Participle of helfen (L2-M1). helfen takes the dative, so it is Ihnen geholfen — the person helped is never an accusative object.

sentences.trap: Both halves are past, and only one is unreal: hätte geholfen for the help that never came, hatte for the missing time that really was missing.
sentences.sound: ikh HET-uh EE-nun gern ge-HOL-fun, AA-ber ikh HAT-uh KAI-nuh TSAIT.

variations.display: Ich hätte dir gern geholfen, aber ich hatte keine Zeit
variations.cue: I would gladly have helped you, but I had no time
variations.changed: The same regret to a friend: Ihnen becomes dir. Nothing else changes, which is the point.

mistake.display: Ich würde Ihnen gern geholfen haben
mistake.why: würde builds no past in German. would have helped is one auxiliary in the subjunctive — hätte geholfen — and the three-word English shape has no German twin.

sentences.usage: Declining, after the fact, in a way that keeps the relationship.
sentences.mnemonic: hätte and hatte in one sentence: one umlaut apart, one world apart.
